skill.name: lark-whiteboard-cli
skill.description: Guides AI agents through creating, rendering, and optionally uploading Lark whiteboard diagrams with the whiteboard-cli.
skill.summary: Create Lark whiteboard diagrams from structured requests using whiteboard-cli, Mermaid, and scene-specific layout guidance.
skill.author: larksuite

security_audit.summary: Most high-entropy, path traversal, reconnaissance, and Mermaid findings are false positives from Chinese markdown documentation, examples, and relative links. Confirmed risks are the intended command workflows: npm or npx execution, generated Node scripts, and authenticated lark-cli document or whiteboard updates. No prompt injection text was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before package installation or npx execution. Pin versions and avoid automatic -y execution where possible.

remediation.issue: User text in generated JavaScript scripts
remediation.suggestion: Serialize diagram labels with JSON.stringify or read them from a data file. Never interpolate raw user text into executable JavaScript.

remediation.issue: Authenticated Lark document and whiteboard updates
remediation.suggestion: Keep dry-run mandatory. Confirm the target token, identity, and deletion count before running any command that updates remote content.
Write outputs only under timestamped diagram folders and refuse paths outside the working project unless the user approves.

content.value_statement: Teams need clear diagrams inside Lark without hand-building every layout. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through whiteboard-cli workflows for polished visual outputs.
actual_capabilities: Routes diagram requests between DSL and Mermaid workflows based on diagram type and user input.
Provides layout, schema, typography, connector, and color guidance for whiteboard-cli diagrams.
Supports architecture, flowchart, organization, swimlane, comparison, fishbone, chart, funnel, pyramid, and milestone diagrams.
Guides local generation of diagram files and rendered PNG outputs.
Provides optional Lark whiteboard upload steps using authenticated lark-cli commands.
Includes review checks for text clipping, layout balance, connector crossings, and color contrast.
limitations: Requires Node.js 18 or newer and the Lark whiteboard command line tools.
Some workflows create local files and run local commands.
Uploading to Lark requires valid authentication and document permissions.
Mermaid output has limited styling compared with the DSL workflow.

use_cases.title: Document System Architecture
use_cases.description: Create a layered service diagram with grouped components, connectors, and readable styling for engineering reviews.

use_cases.title: Explain Product Workflows
use_cases.description: Turn a business process into a clear flowchart with decisions, states, and concise labels.

use_cases.title: Prepare Lark Collaboration Diagrams
use_cases.description: Generate whiteboard-ready diagrams and optionally upload them to a Lark document after confirmation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Diagram
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple visual.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a simple Lark whiteboard architecture diagram for a web app with frontend, API, database, and cache layers.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Mermaid Input
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Mermaid workflow to render my sequence diagram as a Lark whiteboard PNG. Keep labels short and readable.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Structured Analysis Diagram
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with scene-specific layout rules.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a fishbone diagram for slow checkout performance. Group causes by frontend, backend, database, network, and third-party services.

prompt_templates.title: Render and Upload Safely
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow with Lark upload safeguards.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a detailed onboarding flowchart, render it, then prepare a Lark whiteboard upload. Run a dry run and ask before overwriting anything.

output_examples.input: Create a microservice architecture diagram for checkout.
output_examples.output: A rendered PNG with grouped service layers, connectors, and a short review note about layout and readability.

output_examples.input: Make a Mermaid mind map for a product launch plan.
output_examples.output: A whiteboard-ready mind map image with concise branches for research, build, launch, and follow-up.

output_examples.input: Upload this process diagram to my existing Lark whiteboard.
output_examples.output: A prepared upload workflow that checks the target board first and asks for confirmation before any overwrite.

best_practices: Confirm the diagram type, target audience, and upload destination before running commands.
Use short node labels and move long explanations into nearby notes or legends.
Run the dry-run overwrite check before updating any existing Lark whiteboard.
anti_patterns: Do not run npm install, npx, node scripts, or lark-cli commands without user approval.
Do not paste untrusted text directly into executable JavaScript templates.
Do not overwrite an existing whiteboard without confirming the deletion count and target token.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates Lark whiteboard diagrams, rendered PNG files, and optional upload workflows for Lark documents.

faq.question: Does it require Lark authentication?
faq.answer: Authentication is only required when fetching documents or uploading diagrams to Lark whiteboards.

faq.question: Can it use Mermaid diagrams?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses Mermaid for mind maps, sequence diagrams, class diagrams, pie charts, and explicit Mermaid input.

faq.question: Can it make custom layouts?
faq.answer: Yes. The DSL workflow supports structured layouts, precise positions, connectors, colors, and scene-specific diagram rules.

faq.question: What files can it generate?
faq.answer: It can generate diagram source files, helper scripts for calculated layouts, rendered PNG images, and Mermaid source files.

faq.question: What should users review before upload?
faq.answer: Users should verify the target document, whiteboard token, authentication identity, and any overwrite warning from the dry run.
